items.reasons: The shelf is drawn as a flat front elevation. The top is only a thin 1–2 row wood strip with no lit plane, while the wardrobe and cooler originals show a clear top surface. The bottle rows sit straight on, with no depth on the shelf planks.

It is a flat frontal panel: the green top rail has no top plane and the posts have no depth. The diamond lattice is a noisy green-and-white checker that turns to mush at 1x and reads more like a crate or screen than a fence. In the room it sits as a free-standing box in the middle of the floor.

It is badly under-scaled for a building: the stair hut is cabinet-sized and its door is about 1 tile tall at 2x, smaller than the desk-height originals. It reads as a grey appliance or console with a sign, not a structure you walk into. The roof plane is cluttered with a vent box and stray dark specks.

The elliptical lid and cylinder read correctly in 3/4. The stand slab top is visible as a lit plane, and the legs and cross-brace meet the floor with a ground line. The navy outline and blue-grey ramp match the sofa and cooler originals, and the scale is reasonable.

A brown and red broom strip runs down the right edge and reads as a side face or detached prop outside the locker's footprint. The blue bucket at the bottom is a muddy blob that overlaps the front face. The locker body is a narrow grey slab, with louvres only sketched in.
